facts.statement: The genus Lomasuchus was described by Gasparini and colleagues in 1991.
Lomasuchus lived during the Late Cretaceous Santonian stage in Neuquén Province, western central Argentina.
facts.quote: Lomasuchus is an extinct genus of peirosaurid notosuchian known from the Late Cretaceous (Santonian stage) of Neuquén Province, western central Argentina.

facts.statement: The only known fossil of Lomasuchus is the holotype specimen MOZ 4084 PV, found at the Loma de la Lata locality in Patagonia.
facts.quote: It is known only from the holotype MOZ 4084 PV which was found in the Loma de la Lata locality of the Neuquén Province, Patagonia.

facts.statement: Recent studies place the fossil horizon of Lomasuchus in the Santonian-age Bajo de la Carpa Formation, though it was originally thought to be from the Coniacian-age Plottier Formation.
facts.quote: More recent stratigraphic work on this area identified that horizon as belonging to the younger, Coniacian-age, Plottier Formation of the Rio Neuquén Subgroup. This horizon is currently considered to pertain to the Santonian-age Bajo de la Carpa Formation of the Rio Colorado Subgroup.

facts.statement: Lomasuchus possessed a deep, narrow snout that is characteristic of peirosaurids.
facts.quote: Lomasuchus had a deep, narrow snout characteristic of peirosaurids.

facts.statement: Lomasuchus had compressed, serrated teeth, though they were not as compressed as those in the related genus Peirosaurus.
facts.quote: The serrated teeth were compressed, although not to the extent seen in other related genera such as Peirosaurus.

facts.statement: The genus Lomasuchus gives its name to the subfamily Lomasuchinae within Peirosauridae.
facts.quote: Lomasuchus lends its name to a subfamily of peirosaurids called the Lomasuchinae.

facts.statement: Lomasuchus belongs to the family Peirosauridae.
Lomasuchus is classified as a reptile.
The Paleobiology Database lists the time range for Lomasuchus as the Turonian to Coniacian stages, between 93.9 and 85.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Coniacian (93.9 to 85.7 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Lomasuchus shared morphological similarities with Uberabasuchus, including a narrow snout and a groove at the maxilla-premaxilla contact that held an enlarged fourth mandibular tooth.
rejected.quote: Many similarities can be seen between its morphology and that of the related Uberabasuchus, such as the narrow snout and a groove at the maxilla-premaxilla contact that accommodated for an enlarged fourth mandibular tooth.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'narrow snout and a groove at the maxilla-premaxilla'
